questions.stem:
Sally plays a game in which she can either win or lose.

A turn consists of up to 3 games. On each turn Sally plays the game up to 3 times. If she wins the first 2 games or loses the first 2 games, then she will not play the 3rd game.

• The probability that Sally wins the first game in a turn is 0.7
• If Sally wins a game the probability that she wins the next game is 0.6
• If Sally loses a game the probability that she wins the next game is 0.2

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Use this information to complete the tree diagram on page 3
(3)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find the probability that Sally wins the first 2 games in a turn.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:

A1: cao

The weights, to the nearest kilogram, of a sample of 33 red kangaroos taken in December are summarised in the stem and leaf diagram below.

$\begin{array}{|c|l|c|}\hline \text{Weight (kg)} & & \text{Totals}\\\hline 1 & 6 & (1)\\ 2 & 3\ 6 & (2)\\ 3 & 2\ 4\ 6 & (3)\\ 4 & 2\ 5\ 5\ 6\ 6\ 7\ 8 & (7)\\ 5 & 3\ 4\ 7\ 7\ 7\ 8\ 9\ 9 & (8)\\ 6 & 0\ 2\ 2\ 3\ 3\ 7\ 8 & (7)\\ 7 & 2\ 8 & (2)\\ 8 & 2\ 6 & (2)\\ 9 & 4 & (1)\\\hline\end{array}$

Key: 3 | 2 represents 32 kg

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find
(i) the value of the median
(ii) the value of $Q_1$ and the value of $Q_3$
for the weights of these red kangaroos.
(3)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
For these data an outlier is defined as a value that is

greater than $Q_3+1.5\times(Q_3-Q_1)$

or smaller than $Q_1-1.5\times(Q_3-Q_1)$

(b) Show that there are 2 outliers for these data.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) M1: For use of either $Q_3+1.5(Q_3-Q_1)$ or $Q_1-1.5(Q_3-Q_1)$ ft part (a)
A1ft: For either 90 or 18 ft part (a)
A1*: For identifying both outliers with no incorrect/missing working (This can ft part (a))
Official notes (completeness pass):
- $'63'+1.5('63'-'45')[=90]$ or $'45'-1.5('63'-'45')[=18]$ M1; $=90$ or $=18$ A1ft; 16 and 94 [are outliers]* A1*

parts.label: c
parts.text:
Figure 1 on page 7 shows a box plot for the weights of the same 33 red kangaroos taken in February, earlier in the year.
(c) In the space on Figure 1, draw a box plot to represent the weights of these red kangaroos in December.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) M1: A boxplot drawn with 2 whiskers
A1ft: For $Q_1$, $Q_2$ and $Q_3$ plotted correctly ft part (a)
A1ft: Whiskers drawn at 18 and 90 ft part (b) or 23 and 86
A1: Outliers marked at 16 and 94

parts.label: d
parts.text:
(d) Compare the distribution of the weights of red kangaroos taken in February with the distribution of the weights of red kangaroos taken in December of the same year. You should interpret your comparisons in the context of the question.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) B1ft: The median/$Q_2$ for February is less/lower than the median/$Q_2$ for December oe
B1ft: The IQR/range for February is less/lower than December (allow similar) oe
B1ft: For a correct interpretation of either average or spread e.g.
• on average February weigh less than December oe
• the weights of February are less varied/little change in variability than the weights of December oe
• They weighed more later in the year oe
• Most of the distribution has shifted right, implying that most kangaroos have gained weight but some appear to have lost weight.
(NB Ignore any reference to skew or outliers)

- A correct comparison of medians ft their boxplot drawn or part (a) (No figures are required but if quoted then they need to be correct ft) Must mention the word median/$Q_2$
- A correct comparison of range/IQR ft their boxplot drawn or part (a) (No figures are required but if quoted then they need to be correct ft) Must mention either IQR or range

questions.stem:
(i) Bob shops at a market each week. The event that

Bob buys carrots is denoted by $C$
Bob buys onions is denoted by $O$

At each visit, Bob may buy neither, or one, or both of these items. The probability that

Bob buys carrots is 0.65
Bob does not buy onions is 0.3
Bob buys onions but not carrots is 0.15

The Venn diagram below represents the events $C$ and $O$

where $w$, $x$, $y$ and $z$ are probabilities.

parts.label: i(a)
parts.text:
(a) Find the value of $w$, the value of $x$, the value of $y$ and the value of $z$
(4)

B1: $z=1-0.15-0.55-0.1=0.2$

parts.label: i(b)

(1)

eq'x'$ or $ rac{'x'}{'w+x'}

Given that

$\mathrm{P}(F)=\frac{2}{7}$ $\mathrm{P}(H)=\frac{1}{4}$ $\mathrm{P}(F\cup G)=\frac{5}{8}$

(a) find $\mathrm{P}(F\cup H)$

questions.stem:
The weights, $X$ grams, of a particular variety of fruit are normally distributed with

$X\sim \mathrm{N}(210,25^2)$

A fruit of this variety is selected at random.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Show that the probability that the weight of this fruit is less than 240 grams is 0.8849
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) M1: $\mathrm{P}(X<240)=\mathrm{P}\left(Z<\frac{240-210}{25}\right)\big[=\mathrm{P}(Z<1.2)\big]$
A1*: $=0.8849$ Cao. As the answer is given then no incorrect working should be seen
Official notes (completeness pass):
- For standardising using 240, 210 and 25

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find the probability that the weight of this fruit is between 190 grams and 240 grams.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) M1: $\mathrm{P}(190<X<240)=0.8849-\mathrm{P}\left(Z<\frac{190-210}{25}\right)\big[=0.8849-\mathrm{P}(Z<-0.8)\big]$ May be implied by $\Phi(1.2)+\Phi(0.8)-1$ or $0.8849+0.7881-1$
A1: awrt 0.673
Official notes (completeness pass):

- $0.8849-0.2119=0.673$ awrt 0.673 A1
